A_general.open_code_note: The official repository is an overview/README, not server implementation. The public vercel/mcp-adapter repository is a general framework adapter, not code identified as the hosted Vercel MCP implementation. Neither establishes deployed server internals.
A_general.mcp_protocol_version: The documentation describes 2025-06-18 Authorization and Streamable HTTP; a 2026-07-31 changelog says the hosted server supports the 2026-07-28 specification and serves both protocol versions at one endpoint.
A_general.mcp_sdk_and_version: NOT FOUND for the hosted Vercel MCP implementation. The 2026-07-31 changelog mentions official MCP SDK v2 and mcp-handler 2.x as the implementation used for the protocol update.
A_general.license: N/A for the overview repository; no hosted server implementation/license identified.
other_official_servers: https://mcp.vercel.com/<teamSlug>/<projectSlug> — documented project-specific endpoint addressing; the tools reference says tool availability can vary by server configuration and team/project scope.
Vercel's general MCP adapter and documentation-site MCP examples are separate products/frameworks, not the hosted Vercel platform server.
A_general.commit_note: commit hash/date filled in by the research script (latest commit on the default branch)

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: Vercel says the MCP server is available on all plans. Access to individual product operations may require a paid plan, billing role, or payment method.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Vercel offers Hobby, Pro, and Enterprise plans; consult the current official pricing page for plan prices and included usage. The MCP documentation does not charge separately for MCP access.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: MCP access is documented as available on all plans. Some actions purchase paid Vercel products or add-ons; the purchase announcement says MCP quotes price and whether a charge is one-time or recurring and completes purchase only after confirmation.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Requires Vercel OAuth sign-in, consent for each client connection, team access grants, and the user's existing Vercel permissions. Some operations require billing access, a valid payment method, a paid v0 plan, or Enterprise. Vercel says it supports reviewed/approved clients; actual tool visibility varies by configuration, client support, OAuth grant, and team/project scope.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Vercel controls supported clients and server configuration; users authorize client connections; organization/team administrators control membership and role permissions; product plans and billing requirements are Vercel-controlled.

C_capabilities.depends_on_mcp_version: Hosted docs describe 2025 protocol behavior; changelog reports support for 2026-07-28 and 2025 clients.
C_capabilities.description_what_how: The official tool reference documents 217 catalog tools and 31 workflow/widget tools across 27 categories. It states actual availability and schemas can vary by connection, server configuration, client support, OAuth grant, and team/project scope. The parsed official category pages expose 248 tool names; see action_count_comment and actions.json.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Tool results depend on the operation; individual reference pages document result formats. The public hosted endpoint requires OAuth, so no authenticated tools/list output was available in the evidence set.

C_capabilities.depends_on_mcp_version: The endpoint presents OAuth protected-resource metadata; hosted docs describe OAuth and MCP Authorization.
C_capabilities.description_what_how: The endpoint returned HTTP 401 with WWW-Authenticate Bearer error="invalid_token", error_description="No authorization provided", resource_metadata="https://mcp.vercel.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource". Protected-resource metadata: resource https://mcp.vercel.com/; authorization server https://vercel.com; scopes_supported ["openid"]. Authorization-server metadata lists DCR registration endpoint, authorization-code and device-code endpoints, PKCE S256, grant types authorization_code, client_credentials, refresh_token, urn:vercel:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code; token auth methods client_secret_basic, client_secret_post, client_secret_jwt, private_key_jwt, urn:vercel:params:oauth:client-assertion-type:oidc-bearer, none; revocation endpoint present. Token lifetime not stated. Server docs say users consent per client and grant team access; existing Vercel permissions apply.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Unauthenticated endpoint response is JSON {"error":"invalid_token","error_description":"No authorization provided"}. OAuth metadata is JSON. Tool responses are operation-specific.
C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: Metadata Doc; Dynamic Client Registration supported (registration_endpoint https://api.vercel.com/login/oauth/register); grant types authorization_code, client_credentials, refresh_token, urn:vercel:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code; PKCE S256; token endpoint https://api.vercel.com/login/oauth/token; token auth methods client_secret_basic, client_secret_post, client_secret_jwt, private_key_jwt, urn:vercel:params:oauth:client-assertion-type:oidc-bearer, none; revocation endpoint https://api.vercel.com/login/oauth/token/revoke; scopes_supported at protected resource: ["openid"]; authorization server advertises scopes ["openid","email","profile","offline_access"]; token lifetime NOT FOUND.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. The official catalog contains read operations and many create, update, purchase, deployment, and delete operations. The reference does not publish MCP tool annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint). 2. Purchase announcement says price/recurrence are explained and purchase completes only after confirmation; confirmation enforcement is reported for purchases. General docs recommend human confirmation, not server-enforced for all writes. 3. OAuth authorizes each client connection; users grant team access and existing Vercel permissions apply. Consent per connection is claimed as confused-deputy protection. Protected-resource scopes list only openid; authorization server advertises openid, email, profile, offline_access. Token lifetime not found. 4. Docs describe project-specific paths and configuration/client/team/project-dependent tool visibility. No documented readonly query parameter, tool filter, or sandbox endpoint found. 5. Permission inheritance follows Vercel account/team access. Specific MCP masking or PII exclusion not found. 6. No MCP-specific rate limits, quotas, bulk caps, or per-call fees documented. Individual products may have plan/billing constraints. 7. Hosted validation/correction and unknown-argument handling not documented. 8. MCP request telemetry, audit trail, and opt-out not documented. General Vercel privacy policy applies to Services and AI product information; it is not specific to MCP handling. 9. `submit_feedback` sends user-requested feedback; it is not described as automatic. Tool reference includes no rate/report/survey/feedback names in its enumerated catalog, but separate changelog documents `submit_feedback`. No tool descriptions push upgrades beyond purchase capabilities. 10. Reviewed sources do not document initialize instructions or server-delivered skills. Security and confirmation recommendations are client-facing guidance. 11. Stateful memory affecting later outputs/tools not documented. 12. Standard single global endpoint is documented, with project-specific paths; no sub-server proxy hierarchy found. 13. Catalog includes tools for narrowly scoped platform operations; no documented raw arbitrary API/SQL/script escape hatch found.
behavioural_instructions_to_ai_verbatim: "After an uncertain write, inspect the resource before retrying." — tools reference.
"Your assistant needs access to the team that owns a project before it can work with that project's deployments or logs." — tools reference.
"Vercel MCP quotes the price, explains whether the charge is one-time or recurring, and completes the purchase only after you confirm." — purchase changelog.
"Always enable human confirmation in your workflows to maintain control and prevent unauthorized changes" — security guidance; recommendation to the client/user.
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: One global hosted MCP endpoint is documented, with project-specific URL paths and variable tool availability; no hierarchy of proxied sub-servers was found.

E_aggregated.action_count: 248 official names in category pages; documentation states 217 catalog tools plus 31 workflow/widget tools (248 total). Actual per-connection availability varies.
E_aggregated.action_count_comment: An official tool reference exists at https://vercel.com/docs/agent-resources/vercel-mcp/tools and states 217 catalog tools plus 31 workflow/widget tools. Parsed official category pages contain 248 named tools, matching that stated total. actions.json contains those official names plus 2 catalogue-only names (MartechDB and Claude connector directory, 2026-10); their inclusion is marked third-party and their identity as native endpoint tools is unverified. Agent Discoverability reports 204 tools; the Claude connector page provides its own listing; mcp.tc says it cannot inspect tools behind sign-in; other catalogue counts vary or are not directly comparable. The 248 official list combines catalog and workflow/widget names, while the endpoint's per-client list can differ. The official docs have no full parameter schemas in the top-level listing, but category pages provide parameters.

E_aggregated.token_method: No hosted server source or verbatim complete tools/list and initialize output was available. The public overview README is not the implementation.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: Vercel dashboard and CLI offer operations beyond the audited MCP catalog; documentation explicitly excludes creating AI Gateway API keys, exchanging SSO tokens, importing KMS private keys, and signing KMS messages or tokens. Use the dashboard or CLI for these operations. Exact additional REST/CLI operations outside the catalog were not exhaustively enumerated.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Vercel advises users to review permissions, guard against prompt injection, and enable human confirmation in workflows. These are recommendations to clients/users except the purchase-specific confirmation statement. It also advises inspecting a resource after uncertain writes before retrying.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Vercel says OAuth connections require explicit user consent per client and that existing Vercel permissions apply. Its AI Product Terms and Privacy Policy govern AI products/services generally; the reviewed terms do not specifically describe Vercel MCP tool-call retention or training. The Privacy Policy states certain de-identified AI Product Information may be disclosed for product improvement and model training subject to team data preferences for Hobby and Pro users.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: Vercel describes the server as providing secure access to Vercel projects; MCP access is available on all plans. The purchase changelog states purchases are confirmed after the price and recurring/one-time nature are explained.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: OAuth metadata verifies the authorization server, registration support, PKCE, grant types, and advertised scopes. Official pages document team permissions and per-connection consent but hosted implementation code was unavailable for independent verification. Purchase confirmation is a documented workflow claim; general human confirmation is user/client guidance. Privacy promises/policies are not shown to be enforced by MCP-specific code.

contradictions: The 2025 documentation describes MCP Authorization and Streamable HTTP for the 2025-06-18 specification; a 2026-07-31 changelog reports support for 2026-07-28 as well, stating both versions share the endpoint.

Protected-resource metadata advertises only the `openid` scope, while the authorization-server metadata advertises `openid`, `email`, `profile`, and `offline_access`; docs describe access to teams/projects without detailing resource scopes.

The reference states 217 catalog tools and 31 workflow/widget tools; extracted category pages yield 248 names, matching their combined total, while some external catalogues report other counts, including Agent Discoverability's 204.

The Claude connector directory and MartechDB list additional names not found in the official category pages; their status as native tools on this endpoint is not established, so they are separated as third-party in actions.json.
observations_for_research: Official documentation exposes a large catalog plus a separate workflow/widget tool set and says each client connection may receive a smaller or different tool list.
The OAuth resource metadata has only the `openid` protected-resource scope even though the authorization server lists additional identity/offline scopes.
Purchase confirmation is presented as part of the purchase flow; the general confirmation guidance is phrased as advice for client workflows.
A dedicated feedback tool permits user-requested transmission of structured interaction context to the vendor.
notes: Checked the prepared links.json, links_check.txt, pages/ and local repository copies first. The official repository is documentation/overview rather than the hosted server implementation; the local mcp-adapter repository is a general adapter. The endpoint's `/install` returned 404 and its root returned 401 without credentials, so no authenticated tools/list or initialize instructions were obtained. Official tool-reference category pages were parsed; external catalogue warnings were not relied on for the 248 official entries. Two catalogue-only names are included in actions.json as unverified additions. Pricing page was consulted for plan context; no MCP-specific paid access price was found. OAuth data is taken from the supplied pre-fetched responses.
